title: Make the scale harness settle on two quiet read windows, not one
body:
## Summary
renderLayerAtScale/settle() in console/testing/scaleSmoke.tsx returns after ONE 120 ms window with no new read; on a loaded machine the last answer reaches React after it, so every scale suite can snapshot half a load.

## Description
settle() (apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/testing/scaleSmoke.tsx:78) loops while readBudget.total changed or inFlight>0 over one 120 ms sleep. When the event loop stalls past the mock IPC delay (apps/desktop/client/src/mock/backend.ts:1463, 40 ms) and the window timer together, the read resolves, the query layer queues its notify on a timer that runs after the already-due window timer, and settle returns with the answer not yet rendered. apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/world.test.tsx:48 already learned this (two quiet windows). This round fixed the two carried flakes test-locally (latest.test.tsx waits for the strip; stagger.test.tsx settles twice) because the harness belongs to console-framework; the harness fix covers every other suite that reads right after renderLayerAtScale (a11y, perf, layer smoke).

## Flow
- busy machine (full suite) -> renderLayerAtScale -> settle sees one quiet window -> returns
- the test reads the DOM or the read budget -> a wave-0 action or a strip is not there yet -> red (stagger book,small: actions expected 1, got 0)
- fix: two consecutive quiet windows (as world.test quiet()), inFlight<=0 read as quiet after resetReadBudget

## Expected impact
Scale suites stop flaking under load; about 120 ms more per renderLayerAtScale. Could only break a timing budget near its limit (expectLayerHealthy ms is taken before settle).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - scale suites read a settled window
Before: flake2.sh (latest + stagger beside a parallel 4-directory vitest load): 1/8 runs red (stagger.test.tsx:196 book,small) with the one-window settle
After: test-local double settle measured this round (see the round reply); the harness-level change not measured
Method: experiment - the same load loop on both arms; the harness file is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/testing/scaleSmoke.tsx:78-84 (one window)
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/world.test.tsx:48-59 (two windows, the lesson)
flake-before2 run 6: AssertionError: the action was there in wave 0: expected 1 to be +0 (stagger.test.tsx:196)
instrument: 10 runs of latest.test.tsx + stagger.test.tsx beside `vitest run src/windows/approval src/windows/main/console/areas src/shared src/windows/tumbler`; arm A = harness as is with the test-local waits reverted, arm B = two-window settle

title: Find with an empty query never lists a place once a wallet has ~34 deals
body:
## Summary
searchIndex caps at FIND_CAP=40 in group order needs > modules > deals > places, so on any busy wallet the 11 places (Settings, Connections, Quit...) are cut from the empty Find, and the footer says "40 shown" without saying more exist.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/findIndex.ts:169-177 walks FIND_ORDER and stops at the cap; apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/Find.tsx:24-36 lists 11 places last. With needs + 6 modules + deals >= 40 (every ?scale=large world: 500 deals) an empty Find shows no place, though Find is the documented way to reach them ("/ Find a deal, a person or a place"). findShown(items.length) (apps/desktop/client/src/lib/words.ts:1053) prints "40 shown" with no total. Fixed: an empty query keeps a few rows per group (or the places before the long deal tail), and the count names the total.

## Flow
- open ?scale=large -> press / -> empty Find
- needs, 6 modules, then deals fill the 40 rows -> no Settings, no Quit
- type "settings" -> found; nothing told the owner to type

## Expected impact
The owner sees every kind of target the moment Find opens. Risk: findIndex.test.ts pins the old ranking.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - places reachable from an empty Find
Before: places on the empty Find at ?scale=large: 0 of 11 (6 modules + 500 deals > cap 40)
After: not measured: needs a ranking choice (per-group quota vs order)
Method: simulation - three cases: scale large (0/11), scale small (fewer than 34 deals: some places), first run (all places)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: a Find test on renderLayerAtScale(home, large): press /, assert a places-group row (Settings) is listed and the count names the total

title: Move QuitSheet off useWorld() and delete the deprecated whole-World hook
body:
## Summary
QuitSheet.tsx:19 is the last useWorld() consumer (this round moved Status.tsx off it); with it gone, world.tsx can drop useWorld and its second context.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/world.tsx:94-100 keeps useWorld() ("deprecated: new views select") and provides Ctx beside StoreCtx for it. After a71cdce the only consumer is apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/QuitSheet.tsx:19 (deals + display for row names). useDeals() + useWorldSelector(w => w.display) cover it; then Ctx and useWorld go. docs/build/CLIENT-V2-PORT.md:31 mentions useWorld() and needs a line.

## Flow
- QuitSheet: useDeals + a display selector
- world.tsx: delete useWorld and Ctx.Provider
- docs/build/CLIENT-V2-PORT.md: one line

## Expected impact
One context provider fewer re-rendering on every World change; the deprecation becomes a deletion. Nothing visible changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - deprecated API removed
Before: useWorld() consumers: 1 (QuitSheet.tsx:19)
After: 0, hook deleted
Method: probe - git grep "useWorld()" outside world.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none

title: An invoice decision is owned by Book in Rust and dropped by the bead strip
body:
## Summary
table-attention maps DealKind::Invoice to Module::Book, logic.moduleOf lets the attention item win, and BeadStrip draws no Book segment: an invoice that needs the owner vanishes from the strip while the strip label still counts it.

## Description
crates/table-attention/src/lib.rs:159 Invoice => Module::Book. apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/logic.ts:5-11 documents "Book owns no deals" and maps invoice -> rescue, but rule 1 (attention wins) returns book. apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/BeadStrip.tsx:46 filters book out, :35 pushes the bead into the book list, :45 counts needs across every list including book, so stripLabel(all, needs) names one more needs-you than there are beads. The Rescue tab count (apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/Console.tsx:370) also drops the invoice while it waits. Fixed: one owner for invoices on both sides (rescue, per the client contract) or a Book segment.

## Flow
- an invoice deal gets an attention item (module book)
- world.moduleOfDeal -> book
- BeadStrip: bead in the book list, not drawn; the label counts it
- attention clears -> the deal jumps to rescue

## Expected impact
The needs-you count and the beads agree; the deal stays in one module. A Rust change touches the attention projection's other readers (approval window, tumbler).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every needs-you deal has a bead
Before: an invoice needing the owner: 0 beads, counted 1 in the label (walked from code)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - code path walked; no mock world raises an invoice attention item
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: BeadStrip test: a World with one invoice deal + an AttentionItem {module: book}; assert one bead drawn and the label's needs equal the beads

title: Retire legacy .amt and the console.css rule that exists only to undo it
body:
## Summary
legacy.css .amt (font 600 1.05rem display, right-aligned) reaches v2 amounts (Centre title em.amt, Waiting rows, shared/ui/story.tsx); console.css:88 resets font-size, weight and alignment on .cs-centre/.cs-waiting just to cancel it.

## Description
A rule and its counter-rule: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/legacy.css:21 styles every .amt in the main window; apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/console.css:88 ".cs-centre .amt, .cs-waiting .amt { font-size: inherit; font-weight: inherit; text-align: inherit; }" undoes it on two surfaces; other .amt users (apps/desktop/client/src/shared/ui/story.tsx:101; ui-row amounts via apps/desktop/client/src/design/ui.css:90) get part of it. legacy.test.ts counts .amt as drawn (v2 parts draw it), so this needs a visual check, not the dead-rule gate.

## Flow
- delete legacy .amt, .amt small, .amt.big, .amt.struck
- delete console.css:88
- computed-style probe of Centre, Waiting and a deal story at 1280x800, both arms

## Expected impact
Two rules fewer and no hidden cascade on money text. Risk: an .amt outside the two reset surfaces changes font.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no legacy cascade on v2 money
Before: rules touching v2 .amt: legacy 4 + reset 1
After: 0
Method: simulation - grep of drawers; jsdom has no layout
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Playwright computed-style probe (font, size, text-align) of .amt on Centre, Waiting and the deal story, both arms

title: Move the main window shell's inline copy into lib/words
body:
## Summary
About 57 owner-facing strings in the shell sit inline (Shortcuts groups, Find place subtitles, Status chips, QuitSheet, quit.ts, paletteCopy.ts, ui.tsx Loading) though the UX-GUIDE checklist says strings live in lib/words.

## Description
docs/ux/UX-GUIDE.md checklist: "Strings live in lib/words.ts or the area's lib/words/<area>.ts, and the area's words guard passes". Inline today: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/Shortcuts.tsx GROUPS (~23), apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/Find.tsx:25-35 place subtitles and "Quit The Table" (5), apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/Status.tsx (~16), apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/QuitSheet.tsx (5), apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/quit.ts:176-180 (5), apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/paletteCopy.ts (2), apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/ui.tsx:40 (1). "Quit The Table" is spelled separately in Find.tsx:35 and QuitSheet.tsx.

## Flow
- add the shell's words (lib/words/framework.ts or a shell file)
- replace the inline strings
- extend a words guard to these files

## Expected impact
One place to change wording; the words guard covers the shell. lib/words is a shared surface: one immediate commit.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - copy in one place
Before: inline owner-facing strings in the shell: ~57
After: 0
Method: probe - read of the 7 files
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a words-guard test over JSX text and string props of these files (inline count -> 0)
